title: Islanded kernel shadowwork — weekly log
content:
Summary:
Quick capture from the Friday sync and the late-night shadow run. This week we ran a partial islanded shadow of the new kernel handshake + KV shadowing layer against a steady 120qps arrival shape (90p95 bursts). Purpose: validate KV sticky entries under churn and measure batch jitter when coalescer introduces late arrivals.

High-level outcomes:
- Kernel handshake change (two-way ACK window) reduced cold-kernel start stalls by ~18% on the synthetic tail workload but introduced a new path where KV lookups were sometimes deferred for up to +6ms.
- KV sticky entries: hotset retention improved after small TTL bump; however we observed a correlated spike in eviction thrash when arrivals included many short-lived conversations (median tokens < 12).
- Microbatch jitter: coalescer changes to wait-for-raft-slot (experimental) reduced average per-token cpu by 7% in stable windows but increased 99th percentile latency by ~9% for sub-30ms requests.

Logs / notable incidents:
- 2029-03-12 01:12 UTC: shadow node kernel-isl-07 reported repeated handshake mismatches during a config roll; auto-fallback triggered and route moved to kernel-isl-02. Root cause: race between prefill invalidation and handshake rewrite (SRV-9274).
- 2029-03-13 04:03 UTC: KV cache observed a short thrashing window when many chat sessions reopened concurrently (customer-sim v3). Memory pressure triggered reactive eviction policy; no SLA violations but unit cost delta noticed.

Detailed observations:
1) Kernel handshake (two-way ack)
- Why: reduce wasted kernel launches and double-allocs when clients speculatively prefill and then cancel.
- What changed: handshake now waits for confirmation token from runtime before committing thin-state. Two extra micro-op checks added (~0.4ms steady).
- Results: cold-start stall reduction in bench harness for sequences > 64 tokens. But in live shadow with KV enabled, we saw deferred KV probes because handshake holds a tiny lock while reconciling prefill status.
- Hypothesis: the lock contention happens when prefill coalescer triggers concurrent invalidations; need finer-grained invalidation token.

2) KV cache sticky-ttl test
- Test config: baseline ttl=120s, trial ttl=180s, shadow run 24h.
- Hotset hit-rate: baseline 72% -> trial 83% (for steady customers).
- Eviction thrash: transient increase in evictions by +27% for high-churn traffic patterns.
- Notes: sticky entries help for long-running convos but harm when sessions are ephemeral. Consider TTL adaptive by conversation length or token-distribution.

3) Batching / coalescer behavior
- Tuning: experimental 'wait-for-raft-slot' gating enabled; coalescer waits up to 2ms for a matching arrival before emitting a microbatch.
- Pros: more contiguous batches, lower per-token CPU for medium payloads.
- Cons: adds additional tail latency for top percentile; customers with strict <30ms SLOs see larger regressions.
- Action: limit wait window dynamically per route based on SLO tier. Implemented proto: SRV-9318.

Metrics snapshot (shadow nodes, averages across 48h window):
- QPS (shadowed): 120
- median latency: 14.2ms
- p95 latency: 42.8ms
- p99 latency: 117.3ms
- KV hit-rate (trial): 81%
- kernel cold start stalls/day: baseline 43 -> trial 35
- eviction ops/sec (peak churn windows): 880 -> 1120 (trial)

Action items (owners & rough ETA):
- Add invalidation-token per-prefill to remove coarse lock (Priya Rao) — due 2029-03-19 — JIRA SRV-9274
- Instrument fine-grained KV probe timing in handshake path (Ethan Kim) — due 2029-03-16 — PR linked in artifacts
- Implement route-tiered coalescer wait policy (prototype) (Sofia Alvarez + Janelle Park) — spike complete, rollout early canary 2029-03-20 — JIRA SRV-9318
- Run targeted ephemeral-session workload (short convos median 8 tokens) for 72h to observe eviction patterns (Liam O'Connor) — start 2029-03-15

Open questions / discussion points:
- Should sticky TTL be adaptive per-customer or per-route? tradeoffs between memory/cost and tail latency.
- Can we move KV probe out-of-band for prefills and accept slightly stale entries on first token to avoid handshake blocking?
- Is the cost of extra per-request checks in handshake acceptable for Dedicated customers who prefer stability over micro-latency?

Roadmap for next week:
- Short-term: deploy invalidation-token change to shadow pool and re-run 24h churn test.
- Medium-term: build a small ML classifier (heuristic) to decide sticky-ttl based on recent token distribution for a conversation.
- Ops: add a lightweight alert for eviction-thrash ratio crossing 20% for a node cluster.

Meeting attendees (Fri sync): Sofia Alvarez (owner), Priya Rao, Ethan Kim, Liam O'Connor, Janelle Park, Marcus Liu (oncall).

Notes-to-self / quick TODOs:
- add the microtrace for handshake->kv probe path to the PR description (done)
- link the synthetic workload definition in confluence
- check with product about Dedicated customers wanting handshake off by default for their tier

Raw snippets / heuristics tried (brain dump):
- TTL heuristic: if avg tokens/session > 30 across last 1h, bump ttl *= 1.5; else ttl = baseline. Needs smoothing.
- Coalescer: use exponentially decaying wait window keyed by route load estimate rather than constant 2ms.
- Prefill out-of-band: try optimistic prefill where we accept stale KV for first token then revalidate async.

Closing: this felt like a productive small-island smoke test. The kernel changes are promising but interact nontrivially with caching. Priority for next week is to remove the coarse invalidation lock and re-measure.

References: see linked artifacts above.

-- Sofia
